title: Comparison of finite-field and prime-field Artin–Schreier character sheaves
statement:
Let $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with $q=p^r$, where $p$ is prime and $r\geq1$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and put $L=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Fix a nontrivial additive character $\Psi:(\mathbf F_p,+)\to L^\times$. For every nontrivial additive character $\psi:(k_0,+)\to L^\times$ there is a unique $b\in k_0^\times$ such that $\psi(c)=\Psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}(bc))$ for all $c\in k_0$.

For this $b$, let $X$ be any separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme and $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Let $\pi_q:Y_q=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X[y]/(y^q-y-f)\to X$, with translations $\sigma_c:y\mapsto y+c$ for $c\in k_0$, and let $\pi_{p,b}:Y_{p,b}=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal O_X[t]/(t^p-t-bf)\to X$, with translations $\tau_d:t\mapsto t+d$ for $d\in\mathbf F_p$. In the category of lisse $L$-sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], there is an isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{im}\left(\frac1q\sum_{c\in k_0}\psi(-c)\sigma_c:\pi_{q*}L\to\pi_{q*}L\right)
\ \simeq\
\operatorname{im}\left(\frac1p\sum_{d\in\mathbf F_p}\Psi(-d)\tau_d:\pi_{p,b*}L\to\pi_{p,b*}L\right).
$$
Here constant sheaves are denoted by $L$, and translations act by pullback. Thus the degree-$q$ Artin–Schreier sheaf $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}$ of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] is the prime-degree $\Psi$-character sheaf for the function $bf$. The isomorphism commutes with pullback along morphisms of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes (with $f$ pulled back).

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: character sheaves by pushout of the Lang torsor; agent-written trace-polynomial comparison with the prime-degree presentation

proof.text: Every element of $k_0$ has additive order $p$, so every additive character $\psi:(k_0,+)\to L^\times$ takes values in the group $\mu_p(L)$ of $p$-th roots of unity, which is cyclic of order $p$. The fixed nontrivial $\Psi$ is an injective homomorphism $\mathbf F_p\to\mu_p(L)$ (its kernel is a proper subgroup of a group of prime order), hence an isomorphism. Thus $\lambda=\Psi^{-1}\circ\psi:k_0\to\mathbf F_p$ is the unique additive, i.e. $\mathbf F_p$-linear, map with $\psi(c)=\Psi(\lambda(c))$ for all $c$. By the nondegenerate trace pairing [lem-a1-trace-pairing-nondegenerate], the $\mathbf F_p$-linear map $k_0\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf F_p}(k_0,\mathbf F_p)$, $b\mapsto(c\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}(bc))$, has zero kernel, and both sides have $q$ elements, so it is bijective. Hence $\lambda(c)=\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}(bc)$ for a unique $b\in k_0$, i.e. $\psi(c)=\Psi(\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}(bc))$ for a unique $b$; $b=0$ gives the trivial character, so nontriviality of $\psi$ forces $b\ne0$ (this is the parametrization of Laumon (0.2) with $\psi_q=\Psi\circ\operatorname{Tr}$).

source.place: (0.2), p. 135: parametrization of additive characters by the trace character

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-artin-schreier-trace-cover-map] to this $b$, $X$ and $f$: $\pi_q$ is finite étale with $k_0$ acting simply transitively through the $\sigma_c$ on every geometric fibre; $\theta_b:Y_q\to Y_{p,b}$ is an $X$-morphism with $\theta_b\circ\sigma_c=\tau_{\operatorname{Tr}(bc)}\circ\theta_b$, surjective on every geometric fibre; and all of this is compatible with base change along $h:X'\to X$. Apply [lem-fd-as-cover] to the function $bf$ on $X$: $\pi_{p,b}$ is finite étale and $\mathbf F_p$ acts simply transitively through the $\tau_d$ on every geometric fibre.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: pushout of the Lang torsor

proof.text: Stalks and the comparison map. Let $\bar x$ be a geometric point of $X$. By the finite stalk formula [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula], restriction of germs identifies $(\pi_{q*}L)_{\bar x}$ with the space $\operatorname{Map}(Y_{q,\bar x},L)$ of functions on the finite geometric fibre, and $(\pi_{p,b*}L)_{\bar x}$ with $\operatorname{Map}(Y_{p,b,\bar x},L)$ (the stalk of the constant sheaf $L$ at each geometric point is $L$). Restriction of germs is compatible with pullback along morphisms of finite $X$-schemes, so under these identifications $\sigma_c^*$, $\tau_d^*$ act by precomposition with the induced bijections of fibres. Let $\theta_b^*:\pi_{p,b*}L\to\pi_{q*}L$ send a section $s\in L(Y_{p,b}\times_XU)$ over an étale $U\to X$ to $s\circ(\theta_b\times_XU)$; on the stalk at $\bar x$ it is precomposition with the surjective map $\theta_{b,\bar x}:Y_{q,\bar x}\to Y_{p,b,\bar x}$ of step 2, hence injective. Since $\theta_b\circ\sigma_c=\tau_{\operatorname{Tr}(bc)}\circ\theta_b$ we get $\sigma_c^*\theta_b^*=\theta_b^*\tau_{\operatorname{Tr}(bc)}^*$.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: character sheaf as the isotypic part of the pushed-forward Lang torsor; stalk computation written out here

proof.text: Isotypic parts. Put $e_\psi=\frac1q\sum_{c\in k_0}\psi(-c)\sigma_c^*$ and $e_\Psi=\frac1p\sum_{d\in\mathbf F_p}\Psi(-d)\tau_d^*$ ($q$, $p$ are invertible in $L$). Reindexing $c\mapsto c-a$ gives $\sigma_a^*e_\psi=\psi(a)e_\psi$, and $e_\psi$ is the identity on sections $g$ with $\sigma_c^*g=\psi(c)g$ for all $c$; so $\operatorname{im}e_\psi$ is exactly the subsheaf of $\pi_{q*}L$ on which each $\sigma_c^*$ acts by $\psi(c)$, and likewise $\operatorname{im}e_\Psi\subseteq\pi_{p,b*}L$ is the subsheaf on which each $\tau_d^*$ acts by $\Psi(d)$. If $\tau_d^*g=\Psi(d)g$ for all $d$, then by step 3 and step 1 $\sigma_c^*\theta_b^*g=\theta_b^*\tau_{\operatorname{Tr}(bc)}^*g=\Psi(\operatorname{Tr}(bc))\theta_b^*g=\psi(c)\theta_b^*g$. Hence $\theta_b^*$ restricts to an injective morphism $\operatorname{im}e_\Psi\to\operatorname{im}e_\psi$. Stalks are exact, so $(\operatorname{im}e_\psi)_{\bar x}$ is the $\psi$-eigenspace of $k_0$ acting on $\operatorname{Map}(Y_{q,\bar x},L)$; as $Y_{q,\bar x}$ is a $k_0$-torsor (step 2), choosing $y_0$ identifies this with the regular representation, whose $\psi$-eigenspace is the line spanned by $c\cdot y_0\mapsto\psi(c)$. The same holds for $\Psi$ on the $\mathbf F_p$-torsor $Y_{p,b,\bar x}$. An injective linear map between one-dimensional $L$-spaces is bijective; a morphism of sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ bijective on all geometric stalks is an isomorphism. This gives the displayed isomorphism, induced by $\theta_b^*$.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: pushout of the Lang torsor by the character; eigenspace computation written out here

proof.text: Lisseness. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] applied to $\pi_{p,b}$, every point of $X$ has an étale neighbourhood $U$ with $Y_{p,b}\times_XU=\coprod_{j\in J}V_j$, $J$ finite, each $V_j\to U$ an isomorphism. $U$ is locally Noetherian (étale over the finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X$), so we may replace $U$ by the connected component containing the given point; then each $V_j\cong U$ is connected, and each $U$-automorphism $\tau_d\times_XU$ maps each $V_j$ onto a connected open and closed subscheme, i.e. onto some $V_{j'}$. Hence $\pi_{p,b*}L|_U\cong L^J$ is constant, with each $\tau_d^*$ acting by a fixed permutation of $J$, and $\operatorname{im}e_\Psi|_U$, the image of a constant idempotent of $L^J$, is a constant sheaf, of rank one by step 4. So $\operatorname{im}e_\Psi$ is a lisse $L$-sheaf of rank one, and so is $\operatorname{im}e_\psi$ by step 4; the isomorphism is one of lisse $L$-sheaves.

source.place: (1.1.3), pp. 139–140: the pushout is a lisse rank-one sheaf; written out here

proof.text: Identification with [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf] and naturality. In the current definition ([def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf], blueprint main-20261015) $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}=f^*\mathcal L_\psi$, where $\mathcal L_\psi$ is the image of $e_\psi=\frac1q\sum_c\psi(-c)\sigma_c^*$ on $(\mathrm{AS}_q)_*L$ for $\mathrm{AS}_q:\mathbf A^1_{k_0}\to\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, $x\mapsto x^q-x$, and $f$ is viewed as $X\to\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$. The square with $Y_q\to\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ given by $y$ is cartesian ($Y_q=X\times_{f,\mathbf A^1,\mathrm{AS}_q}\mathbf A^1$), compatibly with the translations. By [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] the exchange map $f^*(\mathrm{AS}_q)_*L\to\pi_{q*}L$ is an isomorphism compatible with the stalk formula on both sides; by step 3 the translations act on both stalks by the same precomposition, so the exchange isomorphism intertwines $f^*\sigma_c^*$ with $\sigma_c^*$; as $f^*$ is exact it carries $\operatorname{im}e_\psi$ to $\operatorname{im}e_\psi$, so $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}$ is the left-hand side, and by step 4 it is the prime-degree $\Psi$-character sheaf of $bf$ (for $\psi=\Psi\circ\operatorname{Tr}$, $b=1$, this is the prime-degree presentation of the imported statement of [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf]). For $h:X'\to X$ with $f'=h^*f$, step 2 (base-change clause of [lem-a1-artin-schreier-trace-cover-map]) identifies $Y'_q$, $Y'_{p,b}$, $\sigma'_c$, $\tau'_d$, $\theta'_b$ with base changes; [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] gives $h^*\pi_{q*}L\cong\pi'_{q*}L$ and $h^*\pi_{p,b*}L\cong\pi'_{p,b*}L$ compatibly with the stalk formulas, so on stalks (functions on the same geometric fibres) they intertwine $h^*\theta_b^*$, $h^*\sigma_c^*$, $h^*\tau_d^*$ with $\theta_b'^*$, $\sigma_c'^*$, $\tau_d'^*$. Applying the exact functor $h^*$ to the images, the isomorphism of step 4 for $(X,f)$ pulls back to the one for $(X',f')$.
